clue.text: Group didn't flog as much with one single out

parts.note: to flog is to whip or thrash; 'didn't flog as much' is read as a verb plus a comparison

indicators.note: one of a pair of identical letters is sent out, so only a single copy of it stays

parts.note: 'didn't ... as much' means did it to a smaller degree
one of the two S's where the pieces meet is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone who stopped whipping so often, with one lonely person stepping out.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAT LESS has a doubled S at the join; lose one and you have BEATLES, the Liverpool band.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were the most famous pop band of the sixties, so a musical group is a fair description.

clue.text: Getting up to go? No need on this vessel

definitions.text: Getting up to go? No need on this vessel

parts.words: Getting up to go? No need on this vessel
parts.note: surface: a ship where passengers never have to rise before departure

parts.words: Getting up to go? No need on this vessel
parts.note: setter's reading: a patient need not leave the mattress to relieve themselves, because this receptacle comes to them

explanation.surface: A cruise ship with such relaxed timetables that nobody has to get up early to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' means relieve oneself and 'vessel' is a container, not a boat; the bedridden use one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedpan is a receptacle used by patients confined to their beds, so they never have to rise for the toilet.

clue.text: Confederate supporting a knight from the rear

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means lying underneath, so the confederate goes below the letters above it

parts.note: used as it stands
N is the chess notation for a knight
a confederate is a partner or ally

explanation.surface: A Southern soldier backing up a mounted knight in a battle charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the confederate sits under A and N; 'from the rear' is the cheeky definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes something done by way of the anus, which is literally the body's rear end.

clue.text: China's real anxious to get a piece of England

indicators.note: someone anxious is agitated and unsettled, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: ten letters of fodder, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: The Chinese being genuinely keen to buy up a chunk of English territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; 'China' here is only letters, not a country or crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is one of the historic counties, a region forming part of the English map.

clue.text: Where young kids learn phonetic spelling

definitions.text: Where young kids learn phonetic spelling

parts.words: Where young kids learn phonetic spelling
parts.note: surface: a classroom where children are taught to spell words by their sounds

parts.words: Where young kids learn phonetic spelling
parts.note: setter's reading: the place of learning, itself written the way it is pronounced

explanation.surface: A primary classroom where the teacher drills children in sounding letters out.
explanation.walkthrough: The phonetic spelling belongs to the answer, not the lessons; it recalls Molesworth's 'Down with Skool!', a British comic book about a schoolboy.
explanation.definitionFit: This childish respelling of the ordinary word for an educational institution is written exactly as it sounds.

clue.text: Very different means to keep baby quiet

parts.note: 'so' and 'very' are both intensifiers
something different is other

explanation.surface: A parent trying an unusual method to stop an infant crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very different' wants to be read as one phrase; split it into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A soother is a dummy or pacifier, a rubber teat an infant sucks to calm down.

clue.text: Get out more, having lost yen to be so virtuous

indicators.note: what is lost is taken away, so the yen drops out of the phrase

parts.note: the opposite of getting out is staying in
to get out more is to stay in less
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Advice to a hermit to socialise, losing their longing along the way to become good.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reversing the advice: going out more is the same as staying at home less. Yen, the Japanese currency, supplies the dropped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stainless character carries no moral blemish, a figurative sense for a person of spotless goodness.

clue.text: Line to be observed when firing arrows

definitions.text: Line to be observed when firing arrows

parts.words: Line to be observed when firing arrows
parts.note: surface: the mark archers must stand behind at a shooting range

parts.words: Line to be observed when firing arrows
parts.note: setter's reading: 'arrows' is pub slang for darts, and players throw from behind a marked line

explanation.surface: An archery safety rule about where to stand when shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs darts are called arrows; the answer is the darts line, not an archery one.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the mark on the floor that a darts player must stay behind while throwing.

clue.text: Sound grumpy when a right ass is allowed into hotels

parts.note: the first letter of hotel, which is also its NATO alphabet letter; one of two
used as it stands

indicators.note: being let into somewhere puts the phrase inside the two hotels

parts.note: ass as backside, the rump
R abbreviates right
the first letter of the second hotel

explanation.surface: A cranky guest objecting when an idiot is let into the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass' looks like a fool but means the backside, RUMP; plural 'hotels' gives two H's to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrumph is to make a gruff throat-clearing noise of displeasure, the verb for grumbling audibly.

clue.text: Goes back in to find tenants injecting drug

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the tenants take the drug into them

parts.note: tenants pay rent
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A landlord returning to a flat to discover the occupants shooting up.
explanation.walkthrough: The E goes after the first letter of RENTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to come into a place again, a plain synonym for returning inside.

clue.text: Sketched daughter with rough end of crayon

parts.note: D abbreviates daughter
raw and rough both mean unpolished

indicators.note: only the final letter of the crayon is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A little girl's picture done with a worn-down crayon stub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough end of crayon' reads as one phrase; 'rough' is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn is the past participle of draw, and sketching is a kind of drawing.

clue.text: It's really moving, performing daily in mature setting

definitions.note: a sentence describing the answer rather than a phrase that swaps in for it

parts.note: a performer on stage is on

indicators.note: the daily's work is placed inside the word for mature
a setting surrounds what it holds, as a ring's setting holds a stone

parts.note: to mature is to age
a daily is a cleaning woman, and to char is to do that cleaning

explanation.surface: An emotional show about someone putting on a daily performance in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a charwoman, a cleaner who comes in each day; the surface makes it sound like a daily show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charging is rushing forward at speed, so being on a charge means going fast.

clue.text: Gladly loan novel for 24 hours

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Happily lending someone a book for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book being lent; it is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting the whole day from morning to night, a loose idiom for a full daily span.

clue.text: Short circuit usually ruins the leads

indicators.note: leads are what go in front, so the opening letters of the words are wanted

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words
'the' gives its own first letter too

explanation.surface: An electrician's grumble that a short circuit tends to damage the wires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short circuit' looks like one phrase; 'Short' is the definition and 'the' is part of the fodder as well as the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt reply is brief to the point of rudeness, so it is a synonym for abrupt speech.

clue.text: Supporter who's hopeful when depositing money in spring

definitions.text: who's hopeful when depositing money in spring
definitions.meaning: a person tossing a coin into a wishing well makes a wish

explanation.surface: A fan who saves money each spring in the hope of good things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is a water source, a well, not the season; the second reading takes the compound literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-wisher backs someone by hoping for their success, which is a kind of moral support.

clue.text: Accommodate goalie, one who provides clean sheets, perhaps

definitions.text: one who provides clean sheets, perhaps

parts.note: to house is to accommodate
a goalkeeper is a keeper

explanation.surface: Putting up a football goalkeeper who keeps clean sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a clean sheet is a match without conceding, which a goalie provides; here the sheets are bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic worker running a household changes the bedding, laundering linen as one example of the duties.

clue.text: Natural fungi need scrambling

indicators.note: things that need scrambling are to be mixed up, so the letters get stirred

parts.note: nine letters; 'need' serves as fodder as well as in the indicator

explanation.surface: Organic mushrooms needing to be cooked like eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Need' does double duty, as fodder and as part of the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfeigned feelings are genuine and not pretended, so they come naturally without affectation.

clue.text: Napping when not on screen?

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
a screen shields, as a fireguard does

explanation.surface: Dozing whenever you are not appearing on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' suggests a TV; here it is a protective barrier. To be caught napping is to be caught off guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Napping in the idiom 'caught napping' means unprepared, which is exactly being unready for attack.

clue.text: It's just a messy rip in skin

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the word for skin
something messy is disordered, so those letters are jumbled

parts.note: the rest of the fodder
to flay is to strip the skin off
used as it stands, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Shrugging off an untidy tear in the skin as merely a scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' is not 'merely' but 'fair'; the definition is a whole sentence describing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair play is conduct that is equitable and honest, so it is something just.

clue.text: All staff rue circulating such a blunt denial

indicators.note: circulating things move around, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: eleven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: An office memo turning down a request so bluntly that every employee regrets it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulating' suggests a memo going round the office; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat refusal is an outright no, with flat meaning absolute and unqualified.

clue.text: Position adopted by extremists in secret Aryan clique

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A political line taken by fanatics in a hidden racist group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' paints radicals, but it means the extreme letters of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is an attitude or standpoint taken on an issue, a synonym for an adopted opinion.

clue.text: How to get picture from pure junkie

parts.note: the instruction is to add letters
the letters needed to turn the short word into the long one

explanation.surface: Describing how to make art out of a drug user's pure fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PURE from PICTURE and ICT remains, so to get from one to the other you ADD ICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A junkie is slang for a drug user dependent on a substance, which is one kind of addict.

clue.text: Good basic education can make one sound angry

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase, an angry sound

parts.note: G abbreviates good
the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Grumbling that a decent grounding in schooling can leave someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are the basics of schooling, each spelt with an R sound.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the growling noise people or dogs make when cross, written out as an interjection.

clue.text: Note dashed off could appear this way in the Guardian!

definitions.text: could appear this way in the Guardian!

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
dashed off as in ran off quickly

explanation.surface: A hastily written note that might turn up in this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed off' suggests hasty writing but means ran. The Guardian is famous for its typos, earning the nickname the Grauniad.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper's reputation for typographical errors makes wrongly typeset text a self-mocking description.

clue.text: Quietly, church abandons VIPs for more common people

parts.note: p is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: whatever abandons a group leaves it, so the church letters come out of the VIPs

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
celebrities are VIPs

explanation.surface: The clergy quietly dropping celebrities to minister to ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England; 'for more' just leads into the definition, suggesting the church wants a larger ordinary flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebs is informal British slang for ordinary people, from the plebeians of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Dangerous mountain in Vietnam

indicators.note: the mountain sits inside the letters of the country's name

parts.note: the middle four letters

explanation.surface: A perilous peak in South-East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue places the mountain in Vietnam; it is actually a Sicilian volcano, only hiding there.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano on Sicily, so a hazardous peak that still erupts regularly.

clue.text: Expert garners unbelievable return working so quickly

indicators.note: to garner is to gather in, so the expert takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: returning is going back, so the word for unbelievable runs backwards

parts.note: a tall story is unbelievable
a machine working is on

explanation.surface: A skilled investor making a staggering profit by trading at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unbelievable return' looks like a big profit; it is TALL written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once means suddenly, happening in an instant, which is a matter of great speed.

clue.text: Have noises reduced by half in this city?

indicators.note: each word is cut to its first half, keeping only the front part

parts.note: first half of the word
first half of the word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether this city has cut its noise pollution in half.
explanation.walkthrough: It links to 24 down, placed in Vietnam: this is its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam, a large metropolis in the north of the country.

clue.text: Boring win nervous sailors might long for

parts.note: a dry talk is boring
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A dull victory that anxious seamen would still yearn for.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasick or frightened seamen wish to be ashore, back on solid ground away from waves.

clue.text: Auntie frustrated — she holds back too much

indicators.note: going back runs the letters the opposite way
what is held is contained, so the answer is inside the clue's words

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A frustrated aunt who is too reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is part of the indicator phrase, not fodder; read the letters right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, an amount beyond what is needed or wanted.
